provider: Epic Online Services Player Data Storage

free_tier.stated: 400 MB total storage per user, 200 MB maximum per file, 1,000 files per user. No published product-level or title-level byte cap.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: No per-GB egress meter documented for Player Data Storage; access is metered as API requests. EOS itself is free for all developers.

tooling: EOS SDK (C/C++), C# and Unreal plugins (PlayEveryWare/eos_plugin_for_unity). File ops are chunked read/write callbacks: EOS_PlayerDataStorage_WriteFile / ReadFile / QueryFileList. No rclone backend.
chaining: 400 MB per ProductUserId x unlimited free player identities. EOS supports anonymous/device auth, so identities are mintable at will; each new ProductUserId is a fresh 400 MB bucket. 2,500 identities = 1 TB.
limits_note: Per-object-cap: 200 MB per file and 64-character filename limit; request-rate: ~1,000 read or write requests per minute per user, then EOS_PlayerDataStorage_UserThrottled; per-object-cap: 1,000 files per user. Retention: none stated. Files persist until explicitly deleted; no expiry found. Data is encrypted at rest with a client-side key EOS never stores, so losing the key loses the bytes.
